correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the analytic proof from RESULT.md blob 11cbbd9e649066560233055c60f5cba5e4e3b940. For a product base K, replacing arbitrary test bodies L,M by Cartesian products of their factor projections weakly increases the mixed two-body numerator by monotonicity; their first mixed-volume denominators remain exactly equal because the first area measure of K is carried by factor-normal subspaces and h_L restricted to each is the projected support function. Expanding vol(K+t product(L_i)+s product(M_i))=product_i vol(K_i+t L_i+s M_i) gives normalized coefficients sum a_i, sum b_i and sum_{i≠j}a_i b_j+sum c_i. Each c_i≤[(d_i-1)/d_i] beta_i a_i b_i and all a_i,b_i≥0. Dividing yields upper beta_n≤n/(n-1) Gamma. Tests supported in different factor subspaces attain cross coefficient 1; tests in one factor approximate its beta_i, proving each lower-bound term even if sup is unattained. Symmetric affine invariance holds via determinant normalization. Theorem 6.1 of Soprunov–Zvavitch establishes beta_2(D)≤2, supplying the planar corollary. Inspected the bundled exact polynomial-product and zonotope determinant checker and separately checked the combinatorial coefficient expansion; bounded finite checks are corroboration, not the arbitrary-body proof.
residual_risks: No product law asserted for Minkowski sums, nonproduct bodies, more than two free tests, or unspecified higher-dimensional factor constants.

value.rationale: The optimal two-body Bézout coefficient is a standard geometric invariant, and the exact functorial Cartesian-product law reduces a general higher-dimensional optimization to factor invariants plus one cross-factor witness. It gives a new sharp all-dimension consequence for products of planar sets and segments; such a tensorization statement is mathematically useful even though its proof uses classical mixed-volume tools.
residual_risks: Any novelty claim for special products of simplices should be tempered by pre-existing multihomogeneous Bézout principles.

final_claim: For every Cartesian product K=K_1×···×K_m of at least two full-dimensional convex factors, beta_n(K)=n/(n-1) max{1, max_{i:d_i>=2}[(d_i-1)/d_i] beta_{d_i}(K_i)}; products of segments and planar convex factors have sharp beta_n=n/(n-1).
limitations: The source proof treats compact full-dimensional convex factors, m≥2 and exactly two free test bodies; higher-dimensional beta_i remain input constants.
Full literature search for old product tensorization analogues is incomplete.
